output.title: Transcript Accuracy Is a Workflow Cost, Not a Feature
output.body:
If transcript accuracy matters to your business, the real question is not “is AI good enough?” It is: which recurring transcript task costs you more right now — manual checking, or using a draft that still needs review?

Treat it as a bounded workflow decision. First, name the task: customer-facing meeting notes, internal call summaries, or text pulled from records like invoices. Each has a different tolerance for error. Then ask one plain question: what happens if this is wrong once?

That answer tells you the control you need. If the task affects approvals, keep human approval in the loop. Money movement and other high-risk decisions stay human. If the task is low risk, a draft may be enough. If it sits in high-sensitivity medical, legal, or financial work, that is current scope discipline for Bareni, not a claim that such work can never be automated.

For an owner, the next step is simple: pick one recurring transcript workflow this week and note two things for your own records — the time spent verifying it, and the cost of one mistake. That gives you a threshold you can actually use. Fine is not a control.

If you want, compare that threshold against the current workflow before you change anything.
